281	\label{app:bootstrap}
282	
283	We employ clustered bootstrap resampling to compute 95\% confidence intervals for all reported correlations and effect sizes.
284	The cluster unit is the (fraction, seed) pair, yielding $6 \times 5 = 30$ independent clusters in the full experimental design.
285	Within each bootstrap iteration ($B = 10{,}000$ resamples), we resample clusters with replacement and recompute the statistic of interest.
286	This accounts for the within-run dependence across generations: generation $g+1$ trains on data produced by the model from generation $g$, so observations within a (fraction, seed) run are causally linked.
287	
288	Pooling individual generation observations as independent samples would inflate the effective sample size from 30 to 150, producing artificially narrow intervals.
289	Our clustered approach yields conservative but honest intervals that reflect the true experimental degrees of freedom.

\subsection{Synthetic Data Generation}
\label{app:data_gen}
%% Source: mvp_frac50_100 — generation config

At each generation $g$, we sample synthetic text from the fine-tuned model $\tilde{M}_g$ using the following procedure:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{Prompting:} The first 32 tokens of each randomly subsampled real-text chunk serve as the prompt.
    \item \textbf{Decoding:} Nucleus sampling with temperature $\tau = 1.0$ and top-$p = 0.95$.
    \item \textbf{Max new tokens:} 480 (total sequence length $\leq 512$).
    \item \textbf{Subsample size:} 1{,}500 chunks per generation (from $|\mathcal{D}_\text{real}| = 4{,}916$).
\end{itemize}

\noindent
The fixed prompt length ensures that synthetic and real chunks share distributional overlap at the beginning, isolating divergence to model-generated continuations.

\subsection{Evaluation Details}
\label{app:eval_details}
%% Source: mvp_frac50_100 — evaluation config

\paragraph{HellaSwag evaluation.}
We evaluate HellaSwag~\citep{zellers2019hellaswag} using 1{,}000 randomly sampled instances in 4-choice format.
For each instance, the model scores each candidate continuation by computing its per-token log-likelihood conditioned on the context, selecting the highest-scoring option.
Evaluation is performed at the end of each generation (not at intermediate checkpoints) due to computational cost.

\paragraph{Perplexity and token entropy.}
Both are computed on the held-out WikiText-2 validation set using 100 validation chunks.
Perplexity uses the standard cross-entropy formulation (Eq.~\ref{eq:perplexity}); token entropy averages per-position next-token entropy (Eq.~\ref{eq:token_entropy}) over all positions in the validation set.

\paragraph{Spectral signals.}
Stable rank and spectral entropy are computed from the last-layer hidden-state covariance matrix using 64 validation chunks.
We retain the top-5 singular values for trajectory logging; the full eigenspectrum is used for stable rank and spectral entropy computation.

\subsection{Bootstrap Confidence Intervals}
\label{app:bootstrap}

We employ clustered bootstrap resampling to compute 95\% confidence intervals for all reported correlations and effect sizes.
The cluster unit is the (fraction, seed) pair, yielding $6 \times 5 = 30$ independent clusters in the full experimental design.
Within each bootstrap iteration ($B = 10{,}000$ resamples), we resample clusters with replacement and recompute the statistic of interest.
This accounts for the within-run dependence across generations: generation $g+1$ trains on data produced by the model from generation $g$, so observations within a (fraction, seed) run are causally linked.

Pooling individual generation observations as independent samples would inflate the effective sample size from 30 to 150, producing artificially narrow intervals.
Our clustered approach yields conservative but honest intervals that reflect the true experimental degrees of freedom.
